subject.title: [security] Monthly USD caps omit live prior-month reservations

question: Should monthly reserved-USD enforcement count a live managed lease's full reservation in the current month after it crosses a UTC month boundary, or should Crabbox implement a documented pro-rated reservation model?
rationale: Both choices can repair the bypass, but they encode different operator-facing budget semantics and security/cost boundary behavior, so maintainer intent should set the permanent policy before implementation.

options.title: Count full live reservations
options.body: Treat any currently live managed lease as consuming its full reserved USD for admission control until release, expiry cleanup, or terminalization, while keeping creation-month reporting separate if desired.

options.title: Implement pro-rated enforcement
options.body: Prorate month-spanning reservations into the active month and document the exact accounting model so operators know how caps behave near month boundaries.

options.title: Keep creation-month semantics
options.body: Document monthly caps as creation-month-only reporting/admission and accept that live prior-month reservations do not block new current-month reservations.

recommendation.title: Count full live reservations
recommendation.body: Treat any currently live managed lease as consuming its full reserved USD for admission control until release, expiry cleanup, or terminalization, while keeping creation-month reporting separate if desired.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle introduced the usage/cost-control surface and is the clearest owner for the budget-boundary policy choice.
